  D. SECOND READING – ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 662 – ZONE TEXT
  AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS AND JUNIOR ACCESSORY
  DWELLING UNITS (PLANNING CASE NO. ZTA19-003)

  In October 2019, the State of California adopted multiple bills that amended
  the State Law pertaining to the development of Accessory Dwelling Units
  (ADUs) and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (Junior ADUs). An ADU ordinance
  that is not full in compliance with the amended State law became null and
  void on January 1, 2020. At the January 7, 2020 City Council meeting,
  Ordinance No. 661 was adopted as an Urgency Ordinance by a 5-0 vote.
  Regular Ordinance No. 662 was introduced by a 5-0 vote.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council:

  1. Waive the reading in full; and
  2. Adopt “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California amending Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning) in order to amend the
  zoning definitions and development standards to allow accessory dwelling
  units and junior accessory dwelling units in all zones that allow single or
  multi-family units on-site, consistent with state law”.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 21, 2020  3
   E. RESOLUTION NO. 20-02 – ANNUAL RESOLUTION FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURES DURING CITY EVENTS

  Each year, the City of San Gabriel hosts twelve street events in the Mission
  District and in the San Gabriel Village. These festivals take place primarily
  along Mission Drive, Santa Anita Street, Broadway, and Fairview Avenue. To
  accommodate the events, as well as setup and cleanup, specific street
  segments must be closed to vehicular traffic. Staff is seeking approval for City
  event street closures in one consolidated resolution and to authorize the
  Public Works Director discretion to modify dates and times due to unforeseen
  weather restrictions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-02 authorizing the
  Public Works Director to approve the specific street closures, dates, and times
  for each event.

  F. AMENDMENT NO. 4 TO ATHENS SERVICES CONTRACT AGREEMENT TO
  IMPLEMENT THE REQUIREMENTS OF AB1594

  For many years, the City has contracted with Athens Services to provide
  residential and commercial waste disposal services to the residents and
  businesses of San Gabriel. The City and Athens entered into the Amended and
  Restated Agreement on October 17, 2000, for solid waste, recyclables, yard
  wastes, and other compostable collection services in the City of San Gabriel.
  Amendment No. 4 to the Amended and Restated Agreement will allow Athens
  Services to implement new rate adjustments on residential accounts due to
  the new green waste/ organics recycling requirements of California State
  Assembly Bill 1594 (AB1594) effective January 2020.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the fourth amendment to
  the Agreement and new rate adjustments proposed by Athens Services for its
  services in regards to incorporating the green waste/organics recycling
  requirements of AB1594 not to exceed the rate schedule found as attachment
  B on the staff report.

  G. SELECTIVE TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM GRANT (STEP)
  ACCEPTANCE AND RESOLUTION NO. 20-06 AMENDING THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2019-2020 BUDGET

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 21, 2020  4
   The Police Department has received a renewed grant from the Office of Traffic
  Safety (OTS) to participate in the Selective Traffic Enforcement Program (STEP)
  for Federal Fiscal Year 2020. The grant will reimburse the City for personnel
  overtime costs incurred to participate in this campaign and for the purchase
  of related equipment and training in the sum of $50,000. Resolution No. 20-
  06 would amend the current budget to approve the allocation of funds not
  to exceed to amount of $50,000 to be reimbursed by OTS based on actual
  funds used during the Federal fiscal year grant (October 1, 2019 through
  September 30, 2020).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-06 amending the
  Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Adopted Budget to accept Office of Traffic Safety (OTS)
  grant funds estimated at $50,000 into Estimated Revenue Budget Account
  147-3229 and allocate said funds to Police Department Expenditure Budget
  Account 147-751-000 as required. Funding will be applied to projects as
  outlined in this report, and will be used for overtime costs and the purchase
  of any related equipment.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. UPDATE ON WORK EFFORTS RELATED TO HOUSING POLICY AT THE
  STATE, REGIONAL, AND LOCAL LEVEL

  In recent years, California’s ongoing housing shortage has underlined the
  need for local jurisdictions to revisit their regulatory frameworks governing
  housing production. This report provides an overview of the landscape of
  housing policy at the State and regional level and potential implications for
  San Gabriel as a basis for City Council discussion.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and discuss an update on
  current housing-related work efforts.

I  Development Director Armine Chaparyan, Community

I  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item 4F was pulled by Vice Mayor Menchaca for separate consideration.

I  Regarding item 4F, Vice Mayor Menchaca commented that she and Council Member
  Harrington are still in negotiations with Athens Services, but the item before the City
  Council tonight is strictly to be in compliance with Assembly Bill 5094. Athens has also
  been requested to itemize future invoices so that residents can see that the majority
  of the fees relate to state mandates.

  City Manager Lazzaretto explained that there was a math error on the page included
  with the staff report, only in the first two lines: in the second column under green-
  waste disposal, the page in the staff report says $1.34, and in the revised page it is
  $3.55 and $3.27; the total rate was not changed .

  In response to questions from Mayor Pu, City Manager Lazzaretto confirm that this
  item does not deal with a Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) or an amendment to the
  contract which will be brought for Council consideration at a future time, but comes
  under the extraordinary circumstance provision of the contract.

  In response to questions from Mayor Pu, Christian Warner from Athens Services
  explained that the overall rate went up $2.21 for Curb 90/90 (90 gallons' green waste/

I
  90 gallons mixed waste) curbside service, and for residents with a 60-gallon container,
  it went up $1 .93, and that the related Assembly Bill only pertains to residential green
  waste.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Costanzo
  to approve item 4F as amended with the revised rate sheet.

  In response to a question from Council Member Liao, Mr. Warner explained that
  currently, green waste is used in landfills as part of alternative daily cover (ADC)
  between layers of trash. Pursuant to AB 5094, an unfunded state mandate applicable

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 6  January 21 , 2020

  diversion credit; it will have to be taken to a composting facility to undergo a process
  that takes two to four months. As Athens' composting facility is in Victorville, Athens
  is only asking to recover two additional costs, transportation and processing.

  6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. UPDATE ON WORK EFFORTS RELATED TO HOUSING POLI CY AT THE STATE,
  REGIONAL, AND LOCAL LEVEL

  Presentation was made by Planning Manager Tracy Steinkruger, and Southern
  California Association of Governments (SCAG) Housing and Land-Use Planner
  Ma'Ayn Johnson explained the Regional Housing Needs Assessments (RHNA)
  allocation methodology and process.

  Mayor Pu opened the public comment period.

  Sean McMorris, resident, who also submitted a written comment, advocated for an
  inclusionary housing ordinance that requires units in every project to be affordable
  housing or provides an in-lieu fee option.

I
  There was no one else wishing to speak; therefore, Mayor Pu closed the public
  comment period.

  Discussion included Senate Bill 2 requirements, grant funding, and potential
  projects with a nexus to RHNA requirements; the timeline to update the Housing
  Element of the General Plan; elements of an inclusionary housing ordinance;
  transportation challenges; appealing RHNA numbers; benefits of having a land
  inventory; developer push-back on affordable units; loss of local control;
  hindrances to the density-bonus option for developers; San Gabriel's RHNA
  allocation numbers proportional to other cities' numbers; RHNA methodology; and
  how proposed projects would be handled absent outside funding .

  Mayor Pu requested and received consensus from a majority of the City Council
  for sending a letter of opposition to Senate Bill 50 to Senator Susan Rubio with
  copies to President Pro Tern Toni Atkins, Assemblymember Ed Chau and Assembly
  Speaker Anthony Rendon.

  Mayor Pu requested and received consensus from a majority of the City Council to
  direct staff to bring back an inclusionary housing policy for Council consideration,

I  regardless of SB2 funding .
  Assistant City Manager/Community Development Director Chaparyan provided an
  update on a housing trust fund that has been in the works, spearheaded by the
  Council of Governments: a subcommittee is working on a draft agreement for a
  Joint Powers Authority (JPA) that cities can vote to participate in, which would be
  a funding source. More information is anticipated to be presented to the City
  Council in late March or April 2020.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  January 21 , 2020
   Mayor Pu reported that at the study session just prior to this meeting, the City
  Council gave direction to staff to develop a 100% affordable housing project at the
  site just south of the train tracks at 405 S. Del Mar Avenue.
